clue.text: At crawling speed, a finally vital World War II battle

parts.note: a crawl is about one mile per hour, 1 mph, with the figure 1 written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word vital

explanation.surface: Something crucial in a wartime battle happened at a snail's pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 1 mph with the Roman I for one to get IMPH, then add A and L, the last letter of 'vital', as 'finally' asks. Imphal, in north-east India, was where British and Indian forces turned back the Japanese in 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: Imphal is a city in Manipur, India, scene of a decisive 1944 battle against Japan in the Burma campaign.

clue.text: I had meat brought up for religious leader

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Someone had a meal served to a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ID + HAM, read upwards in the down light. The Mahdi is the redeemer expected in Islam; the title was taken by the Sudanese leader who fought Gordon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief the Mahdi is a guided messianic figure who will appear before the end of time.

clue.text: Coming from garden when groom is excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A bridegroom gets worked up about produce from the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is excited' rearranges WHEN and GROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Home-grown vegetables are raised in one's own plot rather than bought.

clue.text: The pound is good in French capital

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound
bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: Sterling holds up well in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French capital' suggests Paris, but 'French' only belongs to 'good in French', and the capital is Portugal's.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal.

clue.text: Avian pest found in hole produced by faulty mower

parts.note: a gap is a hole or opening

indicators.note: a faulty machine is out of order, so the letters of mower are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A garden pest turns up in a hole left by a broken lawnmower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' signals the anagram of 'mower'. 'Avian pest' looks like a bird that is a nuisance, but it is a pest that lives in birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The gapeworm is a parasitic roundworm living in the windpipes of birds, making them gasp open-beaked.

clue.text: He helped create a diary: Roger got his gems transcribed

indicators.note: transcribed means written out anew, so these four words are rewritten in a different order

explanation.surface: A diarist's collaborator copies out Roger's choicest phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcribed' rearranges ROGER GOT HIS GEMS. The diary is 'The Diary of a Nobody', written with his brother Weedon.
explanation.definitionFit: George Grossmith, Victorian comic actor, co-wrote The Diary of a Nobody with his brother Weedon.

clue.text: Whistle and hum going to a game

parts.note: a ping is a high ringing sound, like the whine of a bullet whistling past
hum and pong are both British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Someone whistling and humming on the way to a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' means a stink, not a tune; PONG is British slang for one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong is the informal name for table tennis.

clue.text: Give birth with some assistance

parts.note: help is assistance

explanation.surface: Deliver a baby with a bit of support from a midwife.
explanation.walkthrough: W for 'with' is a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to bear young, used of dogs and other animals.

clue.text: My best friend embarrassed me

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
me is the voice of the crossword compiler, so it stands for the setter

explanation.surface: My closest companion showed me up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' in a clue is the setter. The dog is man's best friend, and this one is the setter's own.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is called man's best friend, and the red setter is an Irish breed of gun dog.

clue.text: "Tom, be seated!" — it comes out as sign of rejection

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the fairy tale, so Tom leads to his surname

indicators.note: comes out says the word it is removed from what is left of the sitting phrase

parts.note: be seated is an instruction to sit down

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit down, Tom, shows their disapproval by gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized hero of the fairy tale. 'it comes out' takes IT from SIT DOWN, leaving S DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturned thumb is the gesture of disapproval, as said of Roman crowds condemning a gladiator.

clue.text: Wanting goals, is likely to miss header

indicators.note: miss header means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: if someone tends to do something, they are likely to do it

explanation.surface: A team short of goals is apt to miss with headers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss header' drops the T from TENDS. 'Wanting' only joins the football picture: the definition is 'goals' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are aims or objectives, as in 'means to an end', so they are goals.

clue.text: Ferocious row with daughter interfering in decoration

parts.note: a din is a noisy row or racket

indicators.note: interfering in means getting inside, so one letter goes into the middle of the medal word

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: A fierce family quarrel breaks out when the daughter meddles with the decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferocious row' looks like the whole definition, but 'row' gives the first piece. 'interfering in' puts the daughter inside a gong, British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong battle or contest is a fierce, closely fought one.

clue.text: Daddy's favourite?

parts.note: pop is an informal name for one's father
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Which child does father love most?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, POP'S PET becomes a term of endearment, just what a father might call his favourite child.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is a British endearment for a small child or loved one, darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: City house creates repercussion

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A building in the financial district causes knock-on effects.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postal district starts EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound bouncing back, and figuratively a lingering consequence or reverberation.

clue.text: Conservative Republican entertained by rich becomes stout

indicators.note: entertained by means held as a guest inside, so one letter goes into the rich word

parts.note: opulent means rich and lavish

explanation.surface: A Tory politician grows fat when hosted by a wealthy Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts R inside OPULENT after its first letter; C comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent describes someone fat and heavily built.

clue.text: Produce dope, with some hesitation, getting worried

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Someone nervously and hesitantly brings out drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but here it means inside information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring something into being, to create or yield it.

clue.text: Confirmed communist supported ruse, as ordered

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported means placed beneath, holding up the other part
ordered means put in order, so the letters of ruse and as are rearranged

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A dedicated Marxist backed a stratagem, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges RUSE and AS into REASSU; 'supported' places RED below it in the down light. 'Confirmed' looks like 'dyed-in-the-wool', but it means reassured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reassured is to have one's belief made firm again, to have a doubt removed.

clue.text: Head of state and Garter knight captured on film

parts.note: a king is a monarch, head of a state

indicators.note: captured means holding a prisoner inside, so the knight's letters enclose on

parts.note: KG are the letters after the name of a Knight of the Order of the Garter, Britain's senior chivalric order

explanation.surface: A monarch and a senior knight appear in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: KG is the post-nominal of a Knight of the Garter, Britain's oldest order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: King Kong is the 1933 monster film about a giant ape.

clue.text: Artist's sculpture unfinished, with one word of refusal

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the sculpture word is cut off

parts.note: a bronze is a sculpture cast in that metal
I is the Roman numeral for one
no is the word used to refuse

explanation.surface: A painter turns down a half-completed statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts BRONZE to BRONZ; the 's after 'Artist' stands for 'is'. Bronzino was a 16th-century Florentine painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnolo Bronzino was an Italian Mannerist painter at the Medici court.

clue.text: Fanciful tune that's variable

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
Y is an algebraic letter standing for a variable

explanation.surface: A whimsical melody keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra, letters such as X and Y stand for variables.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy ideas or promises are fanciful, insubstantial and impractical, as in 'airy-fairy'.

clue.text: International body recently inequitable?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is an international body
just means very recently, as in 'just arrived'

explanation.surface: The United Nations has lately behaved unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: JUST means 'a moment ago' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust means unfair, the opposite of fair-minded justice.

clue.text: Head missing in funny reflection

indicators.note: head missing tells us the first letter of the funny word is dropped

parts.note: something amusing is funny

explanation.surface: Absent-minded thoughts appear in a comic piece about losing one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head missing' takes the A off AMUSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Musing is pensive thought, so it is quiet contemplation.

clue.text: Empty, as bottle finishes

parts.note: these words describe how the word bottle ends: with the single letter E, which three short words can state

explanation.surface: Nothing left when the bottle is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'bottle' finishes in an E; say that in three words and you have the answer. 'as' is a link and 'Empty' is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and vacuous, lacking any substance.

clue.text: Monotonous rhythm featured in group recital

explanation.surface: A drone of a beat runs through a choir's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A singsong voice rises and falls monotonously; a singsong is also an informal gathering where people sing together.

clue.text: Space agency heading for Leo, being nosy?

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency

indicators.note: heading for asks for the first letter of the word Leo

explanation.surface: The US space agency, prying into the constellation Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosy' usually means prying; here it means having to do with the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means of the nose, and here nosy is used playfully for that sense.

clue.text: In oral, do better than a second class

indicators.note: in oral means the words are taken as they sound when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: to beat someone is to do better than them, so this phrase gives the words beat a

explanation.surface: In a spoken exam, outdo someone placed in the second division.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BEAT A and BETA ('beeta') sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, used as the second grade in marking.

clue.text: I stir, about to get cracking -—— my work is late

indicators.note: cracking means breaking up, so the letters of these words are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stirring themselves to get going on overdue work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' rearranges I STIR and ABOUT. 'Late' means dead, not overdue: this writer's subjects are the deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's obituary writer composes accounts of people who have recently died.

clue.text: County backing keeps knight, oddly absent, in power

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the knight's letters go within the reversed county
backing means the county's short name is read from end to start

parts.note: Herts is the short form of Hertfordshire, an English county north of London

indicators.note: oddly absent means the odd-numbered letters of knight go, leaving the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A county holds on to a knight who has strangely gone missing while in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the county into STREH; 'oddly absent' drops the first, third and fifth letters of 'knight', and 'keeps' places what is left inside, before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is force or might, the capacity to exert it.

clue.text: Very little's drunk

explanation.surface: A tiny person is tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is British slang both for tiny (also tiddler) and for slightly tipsy.
